title: What Does the Bible Say About Gambling? 25 Verses
description: Is gambling a sin? The Bible never uses the word. What it says about greed, easy money, contentment and casting lots, with 25 verses.
keywords: what does the bible say about gambling
summary: The Bible never mentions gambling. The word does not appear in the World English Bible or the King James Version, and neither does dice. The closest practice is casting lots, which appears in 21 verses of the WEB: Israel used lots to divide land and settle disputes (Joshua 18:6, Proverbs 16:33), and Roman soldiers cast lots for Jesus' clothing (Matthew 27:35). What Scripture does address is the heart behind gambling: wealth that comes quickly (Proverbs 13:11, 28:22), the love of money that leads people into many griefs (1 Timothy 6:9-10), and the warning that a person's life does not consist of the abundance of his possessions (Luke 12:15). Christians draw different lines on lotteries and cards, and these are the verses most often brought to the question.

faqs.q: Is gambling a sin according to the Bible?
faqs.a: No verse says gambling is a sin by name. The Bible's warnings are about greed, trusting in riches and chasing wealth that does not come from work (1 Timothy 6:9-10, Proverbs 13:11, Luke 12:15). Many Christians conclude that gambling for profit feeds those problems, and many churches ask members to avoid it. Others see a small, budgeted game as entertainment. Scripture gives the principles, and each person has to apply them.

faqs.q: Is casting lots in the Bible the same as gambling?
faqs.a: Not in purpose. Casting lots in Scripture was a way to make a decision before God, such as dividing the land among the tribes (Joshua 18:6) or choosing Matthias in Acts 1:26, and Proverbs 16:33 says the outcome belongs to Yahweh. Gambling for money is a game of chance played for profit. The Bible's lots are the nearest ancient practice, which is why the question comes up.

faqs.q: What does the Bible say about the lottery?
faqs.a: Nothing directly, since lotteries as we know them did not exist. The verses people apply are Proverbs 13:11 (wealth gained by vanity dwindles, wealth gathered by labor grows), 1 Timothy 6:9-10 on the desire to be rich, and Hebrews 13:5 on keeping life free from the love of money and being content with what you have.

faqs.q: What does the Bible say about greed?
faqs.a: It treats greed as a form of idolatry (Colossians 3:5) and warns that the one who loves money will never have enough (Ecclesiastes 5:10). Jesus told the parable of the rich fool to show that a life is more than possessions (Luke 12:15-21).
